F08 / Stress boundaries

Compute-cost pressure, in history.

Trigger: compute and infrastructure expense strictly above the threshold share of revenue for 4 consecutive comparable quarters (SPECIFICATION FR-14). The 60% default is illustrative and adjustable.

Boundary met: above 60% for 4 consecutive quarters by Q4-2025 (longest run 5). Illustrative trigger, not a viability verdict.

Reported compute and infrastructure expense ÷ revenue by quarter (final prospectus; recomputed from dollar values). The vertical marker shows the threshold (60%); bars are scaled to 260%.

Why crossing it here is not distress

Every 2025 quarter was above 60% while revenue grew more than fivefold and prepaid capacity came online: a deliberate ramp. Continuity into 2026 depends on a composition change (leases and depreciation join the line item in 2026), so the Q4-2025 → Q1-2026 run needs reviewer judgment. CL-025 · CL-024

What is not shown

No forecast, probability, solvency or covenant test. The issuer does not report a task or energy denominator, so this is a financial pressure measure only.

The other two boundaries

Committed-capacity useInsufficient evidence

Below 60% for four quarters?

Not evaluable. The filings disclose no utilization of committed capacity, and delivery schedules are not given per arrangement.

Regional powerInsufficient evidence

Required load above deliverable supply?

Not evaluable. No facility locations, load or documented deliverable supply have been extracted (W6).

Monte Carlo ensembleNo trials yet

Seeded uncertainty runs

Planned after the deterministic model and disclosed input distributions are reviewed (BACKLOG T-030/T-031). No probabilities are presented anywhere on this site.
